<MethodEndpoint
  method={"get"}
  path={"/b/pbl/v2/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Returns the full subscription object for your merchant account.

Poll this endpoint to see activation. The checkout webhook usually arrives while the subscription is still `pending_setup`, because Ottu confirms the first payment on a recurring check, so the status lags the payment: within about 15 minutes in production, and usually a minute or two on the sandbox. Do not hard-code a wait: poll until `status` leaves `pending_setup`. If it is still `pending_setup` well after a successful payment, contact Ottu support with the subscription ID.

To link a webhook to a subscription, read `extra.autopay.subscription_id` in the webhook payload: it is the subscription ID you stored at creation. As a fallback, the webhook's `session_id` equals `setup_session_id` on this object.

While the subscription is `pending_setup`, `card`, `current_cycle`, `next_billing_date`, `amount_variability`, `cycle_interval_days` and `total_cycles` are `null`. Ottu fills them in once the first payment is confirmed. If you did not send `end_date` in the `autopay` block, it is set to the agreement's `expiry_date` at that point, so the subscription ends when the agreement does.

`status`, `card` and `current_cycle` are the three fields worth polling. Together they tell you whether the first payment completed, which card is active and how the latest attempted charge went. `plan_name`, `merchant_reference` and `total_cycles` are read-only: the `autopay` request block has no field for them. `merchant_reference` is your checkout `order_no`.


<pre style={{display:"none"}}>{"curl --location --globoff 'https://sandbox.ottu.net/b/pbl/v2/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/' \\\n--header 'Accept: application/json' \\\n--header 'Authorization: Api-Key YOUR_API_KEY'"}</pre>
